summary:
The flaw is in systemd-gpt-auto-generator, which discovers and mounts GPT
partitions at boot (the report describes Red Hat's confidential-VM
images, where a malicious hypervisor can inject a swap partition). That
generator is shipped only in the systemd binary package. It is not in
libsystemd0, libudev1 or udev: Debian's 257.13-1~deb13u1 builds of those
three contain no file named systemd-gpt-auto-generator.

This entry therefore covers only those three packages. It makes no claim
about the systemd binary package, which does ship the generator (Debian
installs it and masks it only on Ubuntu). Debian marks the CVE
NOT-FOR-US: Red Hat and lists no Debian package as affected. The only
fixed version in the record is a Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 kernel build
(0:6.12.0-264.19.1.el10_3), not a Debian package version.

Scanners that match the CVE to the name "systemd" without scoping it to
Debian (for example from Ubuntu's or Red Hat's records) report it against
libsystemd0 and libudev1.

https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-121876
